title: I made an open source harness where AI agents build a browser game and a human approves each step. Here are 3 games it made, and what broke along the way
author: BlueberryOk2154
selftext:
SpriteForge is a local tool: you describe a game in one sentence, and 11 agents (designer, level designer, pixel artist, programmer, QA playtester and more) build a 2D Phaser game. It pauses at 5 human gates: brief, design, menus, playtest, final. Muse Spark writes the design and code, Muse Image draws the art.
    
    
    Three games it made, playable in the browser:
    - Stormlight Keeper (platformer): https://reviver1234.itch.io/stormlight-keeper
    - Pale Shores (real-time island defence): https://reviver1234.itch.io/pale-shores-three-isle-hold
    - Tiny Kingdom Defense (tower defense): https://reviver1234.itch.io/tiny-kingdom-defense
    
    
    What I learned making them:
    - Models need code checking their work. The agents wrote overlapping HUD text and drew ground tiles as diamonds or cubes on black squares; both passed every check until I added deterministic ones that send the reason back to the agent.
    - An automated playtest isn't a balance test. The bot plays in god mode, so it "won" a game no human could. My own playtests caught it, and the fix took two rounds because "make the squads stronger" made them weaker until I gave exact numbers.
    - Each game cost $1.66–$4.89 in API calls.
    
    
    Open source (MIT): https://github.com/reviver134/spriteforge
    pip install spriteforge; it also runs fully offline with mock models.
    
    
    Happy to answer questions.
